name: Aticaprant
summary: Aticaprant, also known by its developmental codes JNJ-67953964, CERC-501, and LY-2456302, is a κ-opioid receptor (KOR) antagonist which was under development for the treatment of major depressive disorder and other conditions. Aticaprant is taken orally.

pharmacology.text: Aticaprant is a potent, selective, short-acting (i.e., non-"inactivating") antagonist of the KOR (Ki = 0.81 nM vs. 24.0 nM and 155 nM for the μ-opioid receptor (MOR) and δ-opioid receptor (DOR), respectively; approximately 30-fold selectivity for the KOR).

uses.text: Aticaprant, also known by its developmental codes JNJ-67953964, CERC-501, and LY-2456302, is a κ-opioid receptor (KOR) antagonist which was under development for the treatment of major depressive disorder and other conditions. Aticaprant is taken orally. Aticaprant was originally developed by Eli Lilly, was under development by Cerecor for a time, and is now under development by Janssen Pharmaceuticals.

sideEffects.text: Side effects of aticaprant include itching, among others.

fact.en: It blocks the kappa opioid receptor, which the body's own dynorphins act on during stress. Blocking it is being explored as a way to treat depression, the opposite approach to most opioid drugs.
fact.zh: 它阻斷 kappa 鴉片受體，身體自有的強度肽在壓力下便作用於此。阻斷這個受體被探索為治療憂鬱症的方法，這與多數鴉片類藥物的方向正好相反。
fact.zhHans: 它阻断 kappa 鸦片受体，身体自有的强度肽在压力下便作用于此。阻断这个受体被探索为治疗忧郁症的方法，这与多数鸦片类药物的方向正好相反。
